images.note: Object 50989: gelatin silver print, printed 1949, gift of the artist. Contemporary negative (March 1936, Resettlement Administration/FSA pea-pickers' camp at Nipomo, CA); this is a later print of the same negative, documented honestly. Verified 1539x2000, image/jpeg, 613953 bytes. Serves the script's AP exam Q1, which is built around this photograph. No qualifying alt: LOC's FSA scan caps at 821x1024, Getty's print via Google Arts & Culture is 938x1200, NARA catalog API was unreachable.
images.source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
images.title: Migrant Mother, Nipomo, California — Dorothea Lange, March 1936

images.note: NPS Photo from the park's 'Civilian Conservation Corps' history page: men using hand tools to build a cave trail. Contemporary (c. 1935; four CCC camps of 200-250 young men worked the park). Matches the script beat 'The CCC put young men to work: conservation, trails, flood control. About two and a half million of them over the decade.' Verified 6124x3620, image/jpeg, 12516166 bytes. No qualifying alt: a second NPS view (maca_27740-B, pole-carrying, 6054x3588) is the same institution; LOC's CCC photos cap at ~1024px on the long side.
images.source: U.S. National Park Service (Mammoth Cave National Park)
images.title: CCC enrollees building a trail by hand — Mammoth Cave, c. 1935

images.note: TVA's own historic photo (from tva.com 'Our History'), showing Norris Dam under construction with workers and equipment. Contemporary 1930s. Matches the script beat 'The TVA built dams and power lines where private companies wouldn't bother... for a lot of those families it was the first time their homes ever had electric light.' Verified 2048x820, image/jpeg, 420672 bytes. No qualifying alt: LOC's FSA Norris Dam item (2001696150) only has a 150px derivative.
images.title: Norris Dam under construction — Tennessee Valley Authority, 1930s

images.note: V&A object O93825 (image 2006AG1657): gelatin silver print by Walker Evans, 1936. Allie Mae Burroughs's husband Floyd was a cotton sharecropper ('halver') in Hale County, Alabama — the exact class of Southern tenant farmers the script's AAA beat describes being pushed off the land ('The AAA money goes to the landowners, not the people working the soil... They get pushed off'). Contemporary. Verified 1400x1786, image/jpeg, 515424 bytes (server uses chunked encoding, no Content-Length header; full download measured). No qualifying second institution found at the bar.
images.title: Allie Mae Burroughs, Hale County, Alabama — Walker Evans, 1936

images.note: Reuther Library item 4735: members of the Women's Emergency Brigade line the street opposite Chevrolet Plant No. 9, Flint, Michigan, 1937-02-01 (Dorothy Kraus sixth from right). Contemporary with the winter 1936-37 GM sit-down strike the script covers ('Auto workers occupied the General Motors plants instead of picketing outside'). Verified 5574x3687, image/jpeg, 2961234 bytes. No qualifying alt: a second Reuther view (item 3900, pickets with Walter Reuther, 3000x2380) is the same institution; LOC's Sheldon Dick FSA negatives of the Fisher Body plant sit-down cap at ~1024px derivatives.
images.source: Walter P. Reuther Library, Archives of Labor and Urban Affairs, Wayne State University
images.title: Women's Emergency Brigade outside Chevrolet Plant No. 9 — Flint sit-down strike, February 1937

images.note: LOC item musftpphotoprints.200224263: b&w photograph, 6 x 8.5 in., dated 1934, from the Production Records 1934-1943 Photographic Prints File. Contemporary portrait of the Secretary of Labor who 'steered through' the Social Security Act (1935) and was the first woman to hold a Cabinet seat — both script beats. Served via LOC IIIF at 1200px wide. Verified 1200x1942, image/jpeg, 272326 bytes. No qualifying alt: the 1939 LOC photo of Perkins (2016875122) has only small derivatives.
images.title: Portrait of Frances Perkins — 1934
